statement.p: We already know we can do the following problem using u-substitution, with u = \sin(-15 x )

We see that \displaystyle \int \sin^{4} (-15 x) \cos^3(-15 x) \,dx \ is solved similarly, because
the exponent of \cos is odd.
the exponent of \sin is odd.
None of the above
So we'll still use u-substitution with u = \sin(-15 x ), after first rewriting \cos^3 (-15 x) = \cos^2(-15 x) \cos(-15 x ) and using a trig identity.
Select the trigonometric identity needed to solve this problem.
Finally, put it all together to calculate \displaystyle \int \sin^{4}\mathopen{}\left(-15x\right)\cos^{3}\mathopen{}\left(-15x\right) \,dx \ = \

hint.p: The integral involves \sin u and \cos u where the exponent of \cos u is an odd, positive integer, namely, 3. So we factor out a copy of \cos(-15 x) and use the identity \sin^2 u + \cos^2 u = 1 to turn the remaining \cos^2(-15 x) into an expression involving \sin^2(-15 x).

Thus the integral can be rewritten as \int \sin^{4}\mathopen{}\left(-15x\right)\cos^{3}\mathopen{}\left(-15x\right) \, dx = \int \sin^{4} (-15 x) \cos^2(-15 x) \cos(-15 x) \, dx = \int \sin^{4} (-15 x) \bigg(1-\sin^2(-15 x)\bigg) \cos(-15 x) \, dx and we use u-substitution.
Letting u= \sin (-15 x) so du = -15 \cos (-15 x) \, dx and thus \displaystyle dx = \frac{ du}{-15 \cos (-15 x)}.

This turns the integral into \int u^{4} (1-u^2) \cos(-15 x) \, \frac{ du}{-15 \cos (-15 x)} = \frac{1}{-15}\int u^{4} (1-u^2) \, du which can be multiplied out, and then each part integrated by power rule.

solution.p: We factor out a copy of \cos(-15 x) and use the identity \sin^2 u + \cos^2 u = 1 to turn the remaining \cos^2(-15 x) into an expression involving \sin^2(-15 x).
Then we use u-substitution, letting u= \sin (-15 x) so du = -15 \cos (-15 x) \, dx and thus \displaystyle dx = \frac{ du}{-15 \cos (-15 x)}.

p.me: \begin{aligned} \int \sin^{4}\mathopen{}\left(-15x\right)\cos^{3}\mathopen{}\left(-15x\right) \, dx \amp = \int \sin^{4} (-15 x) \cos^2(-15 x) \cos(-15 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = \int \sin^{4} (-15 x) \bigg(1-\sin^2(-15 x)\bigg) \cos(-15 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = \int u^{4} (1-u^2) \cos(-15 x) \, \frac{ du}{-15 \cos (-15 x)} \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{-15}\int u^{4} (1-u^2) \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{-15}\int u^{4} -u^{6} \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{-15} \left[ \frac{u^{5}}{5} - \frac{u^{7}}{7} \right]+C \\\\ \amp = \frac{1}{-15} \left[ \frac{\sin^{5}(-15 x) }{5} - \frac{\sin^{7}(-15 x)}{7} \right]+C \\\\ \end{aligned}

solution.p: The correct trigonometric identity used is E.
